topic.title: Java, the World Wide Web, and Beyond
topic.description: History of Java and its role in modern computing
topic.chapter_title: Introduction to Computers, Programs, and Java

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Discover how Java revolutionized the web and modern computing! We'll explore:

• Java's origin story and why it became a game-changer
• How 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' works in real life
• Java's role in everything from Mars rovers to your favorite apps

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine Java as a universal translator for computers. Just like how a USB drive works on any laptop, Java lets programs run on any device - whether it's a phone, server, or even a Mars rover!

Java started as 'Oak' in 1991, meant for smart toasters and TVs. But when the web exploded in 1995, Java became the perfect tool to make websites interactive. Here's why it's special:

• **Platform Independence**: Like a Swiss Army knife that works everywhere
• **Web Magic**: Powers dynamic websites and online games
• **Enterprise Powerhouse**: Runs banking systems and large-scale apps

Think of Java as the 'Lego blocks' of programming - you can build anything from simple apps to complex systems by snapping together reusable pieces.

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Java was created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems and released in 1995
Java is platform-independent due to the JVM: write once, run anywhere
Java applets brought interactivity to early web pages
Java has evolved from web applets to enterprise servers, Android apps, and cloud computing
Java's security model and garbage collection make it robust for large-scale applications

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Java's 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' makes it uniquely powerful for web and beyond. From smart toasters to Mars rovers - Java runs on 3 billion devices. Practice by creating simple programs that explore Java's history. Ready to dive deeper into Java's web capabilities next.

questions.question: Who created the Java programming language?
questions.explanation: Java was created by James Gosling and his team at Sun Microsystems in the mid-1990s. It was originally designed for interactive television but became popular for web and enterprise applications.

questions.question: What makes Java 'platform-independent'?
options: Java code is compiled to bytecode that runs on any JVM
Java does not need to be compiled
questions.explanation: Java achieves platform independence through its 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' principle. Java source code is compiled to bytecode, which can run on any platform that has a Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
